newsitem.title: USA: Top aide quits House fund-raising probe.
newsitem.headline: Top aide quits House fund-raising probe.

text.p: The chief counsel to the House committee investigating Democratic fund-raising practices quit Wednesday, adding to the troubles that have beset the panel in the past few months.
Chairman Dan Burton accepted the resignation of John Rowley and said that personnel changes would neither slow nor interfere with the progress of the investigation.

The Indiana Republican pointed out that the panel, the Government Reform and Oversight Committee, had a large staff of experienced lawyers and investigators and said their commitment and competence "would ensure the investigation's vigour and quality."

Rowley, who was an assistant U.S. attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia before joining the committee in February, reportedly quit abruptly after repeated clashes with the panel's top investigator.

"I have been unable to implement the standards of professional conduct I have been accustomed to at the United States Attorney's office," he wrote in his letter of resignation, parts of which were published in the New York Times.

The newspaper said Rowley's letter criticised the panel's chief investigator David Bossie, accusing him of "unrelenting" self-promotion. Bossie, who is not a lawyer, joined the House panel after working for the Senate Whitewater committee.
Rowley's resignation is the latest problem to bedevil the panel, which has been plagued by partisan political battles. A date for hearings has not been set.
In addition, Burton recently was given broad power over the subpoena and deposition of witnesses despite Democratic protests that they were being shut out.
The Democratic National Committee called Rowley's resignation "deeply disturbing."

"When a former prosecutor leaves an investigation because he cannot tolerate its lack of professionalism, it calls into question the very integrity of the process," the DNC said in a written statement.
